articles.title: Archaeologists found two young horses buried beside a Bronze Age tomb in Germany; the 3,000-year-old ritual may reveal an ancient sacrifice
articles.summary: Europe News: Archaeologists excavating near Nauendorf in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, have uncovered the remains of two very young horses deliberately buried beside a L.
articles.body: Archaeologists excavating near Nauendorf in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, have uncovered the remains of two very young horses deliberately buried beside a Late Bronze Age burial mound, offering rare evidence of ritual animal sacrifice more than 3,000 years ago. The discovery was made during archaeological investigations ahead of construction of the SuedOstLink electricity transmission line, which exposed a prehistoric landscape containing settlements, graves and other features. At the centre of the find were the remains of a burial mound dating to the beginning of the Late Bronze Age, although the mound itself had long since disappeared beneath the flat landscape. Archaeologists identified its former outline from a circular ditch and found two stone-lined human graves inside the enclosure itself. They then unexpectedly discovered a horse buried in the ditch, followed 11 metres northeast by a second horse placed in the same orientation as the human graves. Both animals were foals only about five to nine months old when they were deliberately deposited.How archaeologists uncovered a forgotten Bronze Age burial moundThe excavation took place at Nauendorf in the northern Saalekreis district as part of archaeological investigations preceding construction of the SuedOstLink electricity transmission route. The wider site contains evidence of a settlement landscape dating from the Late Bronze Age and Iron Age, including house locations, storage pits, oven pits, ditches and a burial ground. Among the earliest features was a burial mound dating to the beginning of the Late Bronze Age.The mound itself was no longer visible as a raised feature because centuries of erosion and agricultural activity had flattened the landscape. Archaeologists could nevertheless identify its former location from the circular ditch surrounding it, with an earthen bridge or entrance surviving on the eastern side. Inside the enclosure were 2 elongated, stone-lined graves. The excavation therefore revealed not simply isolated horse remains, but an unusual concentration of animal and human funerary features within the same archaeological monument.Why the discovery of 2 horses inside the burial monument was unexpectedArchaeologists initially encountered the remains of a horse in a deeper pit cut into the southeastern section of the circular ditch. Such pits can contain later human burials, but in this case the excavation revealed a horse lying on its right side instead. When the excavation area was expanded, researchers discovered a second horse only 11 metres northeast of the first.The second animal had also been deliberately placed on its side and was oriented identically to the 2 stone-lined graves inside the burial mound. The State Office for Heritage Management and Archaeology Saxony-Anhalt describes this alignment as an obvious reference to the graves, providing strong evidence that the horse burial was deliberately connected to the funerary monument rather than being an unrelated animal deposit.Why the 2 animals were probably deliberately sacrificedBoth horses were exceptionally young foals, approximately 5 to 9 months old. Although their skeletons were only partially preserved, particularly because of their young age, the surviving skulls and long bones show that the animals were originally deposited as complete carcasses rather than as selected body parts. Both were lying on their right sides with their limbs naturally bent.One foal has another unusual feature. Its hind-leg bones lie almost parallel to each other, which archaeologists interpret as a possible indication that its body had been bound or constricted around the hindquarters before burial. This remains an interpretation rather than proof of exactly how the animal was handled or killed.Radiocarbon dating places the 2 deposits in essentially the same period. The first foal produced a calibrated date of 1212â1055 BCE, while the second dates to 1211â1052 BCE, both within the beginning of the Late Bronze Age. The State Office describes the discovery as a previously singular example of the ritual deposition of such young horses during this period.Why sacrificing 2 young horses would have been significantHorses had a status in Bronze Age societies that extended well beyond their value as ordinary livestock. The State Office notes that their importance increasingly shifted during the Bronze Age from that of a food animal toward that of a prestige object associated with wealth, mobility, religious beliefs and burial practices. Evidence for this changing status appears in rock art, decorated pottery, bronze objects and elaborate horse harnesses deposited in graves and hoards.That makes the age of the Nauendorf animals particularly significant. A foal only a few months old represented an animal with years of potential economic value ahead of it. Deliberately sacrificing and removing 2 such animals from future use would therefore have represented a meaningful expenditure of resources. The archaeological interpretation is that their sacrifice may reflect the importance of the funerary ritual and potentially the elevated status of the people buried beneath the mound. The exact religious meaning, however, cannot be established from the surviving evidence. The archaeologists can identify the deliberate deposition, the animals' young age, their placement near the mound and their relationship to the human graves, but they cannot reconstruct precisely what the ceremony meant to the people who carried it out.How rare complete Bronze Age horse burials areSaxony-Anhalt already has numerous archaeological finds showing that horses or horse parts could form part of prehistoric funerary practices. The State Office specifically cites discoveries at Esperstedt, Burgsdorf and GroÃpasleben, among other sites.Those discoveries include individual horse bones, skulls and lower-leg bones, as well as combinations of selected skeletal parts. Complete horse burials from this period are considerably rarer. Comparable examples have been reported only sporadically in the neighbouring Lusatian cultural area, where horses associated with funerary practices appear to have been cremated and their remains placed in ceramic vessels. The Nauendorf discovery is therefore unusual not simply because horses were involved, but because 2 very young animals appear to have been deposited as complete carcasses in direct association with the same burial monument.What the 2 foals reveal about Bronze Age beliefsThe discovery provides a rare physical glimpse into how Bronze Age communities connected animals, status and death. The horses were not simply discarded remains: their deliberate placement within the area of the burial mound, their alignment and their young age all point toward a purposeful act.The strongest interpretation from the archaeological evidence is that the animals were sacrificed as part of a ritual connected with the burial monument. Their sacrifice may have expressed the status of the people buried there, accompanied the deceased symbolically or fulfilled another religious purpose that is now impossible to reconstruct.More than 3,000 years later, the 2 foals preserve evidence of that decision in the archaeological record. Their bones show that horses could occupy a place in Bronze Age funerary practice that went far beyond their practical economic value.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. The first foal produced a calibrated date of 1212â1055 BCE, while the second dates to 1211â1052 BCE, both within the beginning of the Late Bronze Age. The State Office describes the discovery as a previously singular example of the ritual deposition of such young horses during this period.Why sacrificing 2 young horses would have been significantHorses had a status in Bronze Age societies that extended well beyond their value as ordinary livestock. The State Office notes that their importance increasingly shifted during the Bronze Age from that of a food animal toward that of a prestige object associated with wealth, mobility, religious beliefs and burial practices. Evidence for this changing status appears in rock art, decorated pottery, bronze objects and elaborate horse harnesses deposited in graves and hoards.That makes the age of the Nauendorf animals particularly significant. A foal only a few months old represented an animal with years of potential economic value ahead of it. Deliberately sacrificing and removing 2 such animals from future use would therefore have represented a meaningful expenditure of resources. The archaeological interpretation is that their sacrifice may reflect the importance of the funerary ritual and potentially the elevated status of the people buried beneath the mound. The exact religious meaning, however, cannot be established from the surviving evidence. The archaeologists can identify the deliberate deposition, the animals' young age, their placement near the mound and their relationship to the human graves, but they cannot reconstruct precisely what the ceremony meant to the people who carried it out.How rare complete Bronze Age horse burials areSaxony-Anhalt already has numerous archaeological finds showing that horses or horse parts could form part of prehistoric funerary practices. The State Office specifically cites discoveries at Esperstedt, Burgsdorf and GroÃpasleben, among other sites.Those discoveries include individual horse bones, skulls and lower-leg bones, as well as combinations of selected skeletal parts. Complete horse burials from this period are considerably rarer. Comparable examples have been reported only sporadically in the neighbouring Lusatian cultural area, where horses associated with funerary practices appear to have been cremated and their remains placed in ceramic vessels. The Nauendorf discovery is therefore unusual not simply because horses were involved, but because 2 very young animals appear to have been deposited as complete carcasses in direct association with the same burial monument.What the 2 foals reveal about Bronze Age beliefsThe discovery provides a rare physical glimpse into how Bronze Age communities connected animals, status and death. The horses were not simply discarded remains: their deliberate placement within the area of the burial mound, their alignment and their young age all point toward a purposeful act.The strongest interpretation from the archaeological evidence is that the animals were sacrificed as part of a ritual connected with the burial monument. Their sacrifice may have expressed the status of the people buried there, accompanied the deceased symbolically or fulfilled another religious purpose that is now impossible to reconstruct.More than 3,000 years later, the 2 foals preserve evidence of that decision in the archaeological record. Their bones show that horses could occupy a place in Bronze Age funerary practice that went far beyond their practical economic value.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: India News: SRINAGAR: Joint teams of security forces arrested eight terror suspects and seized arms, ammunition, and other incriminating material in separate oper.
articles.body: SRINAGAR: Joint teams of security forces arrested eight terror suspects and seized arms, ammunition, and other incriminating material in separate operations in three Kashmir districts.Six arrests were made in south Kashmirâs Shopian district and two in Pulwama, also in south Kashmir. A cache of arms and ammunition was recovered in north Kashmirâs Sopore district, J&K Police said Tuesday, claiming the action had dealt a major blow to terror networks operating in the Union Territory.During a naka check at Shopianâs Heerpora, a joint team of the Army, CRPF and J&K Police intercepted a two-wheeler. Three suspects â Junaid Muzaffar Dar, Aamir Yousaf and Junaid Bashir Dar; all from south Kashmirâs Kulgam district â were arrested after two hand grenades and incriminating posters were recovered from their possession, a police statement said.In a separate operation in Shopian, three terrorist associates â Haris Manzoor, Ashiq Hussain and Arif Ahmad Kumar; all from south Kashmirâs Anantnag district â were arrested by a joint patrolling team of the Armyâs 34RR, CRPF, and local police. Security personnel seized a hand grenade, two AK-47 magazines, 20 rounds and incriminating posters from them, the statement said.In Pulwama, a joint team of the Army and police launched a search operation based on intelligence inputs and arrested two terror suspects with a pistol, hand grenade, and ammunition, an Army statement said.In yet another operation in Soporeâs Manzseer area, a combined team of the Army, police and CRPF seized one AK-series rifle, three magazines, four hand grenades, a huge cache of ammunition, and other war-like stores, the Army statement said, adding that further searches were under way.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Report kept from residents now revealed, shows toxic levels in East Palestine
articles.summary: East Palestine residents participating in a class-action settlement say lawyers suppressed their expert’s environmental report to convince them to take the m...
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — Shortly after the 2023 train derailment and burning of vinyl chloride in East Palestine, Ohio, renowned exposure-warnings expert and industrial hygienist Stephen Petty tested the soil and water for residents.

Petty had been hired by class-action attorneys as their testing expert.

When the attorneys negotiated a $600 million settlement with Norfolk Southern , they did not release Petty's results — even to their own clients.

Nexstar's NewsNation has obtained those results and interviewed Petty.

Never-released report shows contamination, Petty says

Petty told NewsNation there are carcinogens in the soil in East Palestine and that they are "above screening levels, which means you can't walk away from it."

Petty said his testing data, and other data he analyzed, show dioxins and PAHs ( polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons ), some of the most carcinogenic compounds on the planet, at elevated levels.

The levels are above cancer-screening levels set by the EPA , which requires further testing and analysis.

"Somewhere between 50% and 70% of the data points, whether they be for dioxins or PAHs, exceeded screening levels" for cancer, Petty said.

"You have to do something. You have to do further analysis to see what needs to be done from a remediation standpoint. And you also have to do further analysis to determine what it means for people in that environment," Petty said. "There is a problem there."

Independent testing expert Scott Smith also came to test on his own. He said he found elevated levels of dioxin, too. Smith and Petty are both whistleblowers represented by the Government Accountability Project.

"It's astounding in that it was suppressed," he said. "Forty-nine percent of the testing exceeds the EPA cancer screening level. Seventy percent of Stephen Petty's data and analysis shows polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons above the EPA cancer screening level."

"It lines up exactly with my data," he said.

Their own lawyers kept the data from them, residents say

Residents said the story they got from the attorneys in the class-action lawsuit was very different.

"Petty's test results were always really secret," East Palestine resident Beth Kosar said. "They said it would hurt the case."

"They told me that in my home, basically, that the numbers didn't support the outcome of the $600 million," resident Linda Murphy said. "The numbers weren't bad enough. And if they revealed them to the court, the $600 million may not even go through because the contamination levels were not bad enough. There would be no long-term health effects risks."

Murphy shared an audio recording she said was from a meeting with the lawyers. In the recording, the speakers can be heard saying, "The data is nowhere near as bad as we thought it was going to be when this first happened."

The speaker also said, "It's almost unprovably bad, specifically for medical monitoring, showing that people have been exposed at a certain level so as to require 10, 20 years of diagnostic testing. Virtually unprovable for any long-term chronic future illness like cancer."

They also said, "The chemicals did not persist long enough at quantities that will expose people over the necessary period of time to produce long-term health effects that are associated directly to this exposure."

Austin Druckenbrod, another East Palestine resident, said he asked the lawyers directly about the tests: "I asked him when I was concerned about the testing they had, that it may not have been the truth. And he said, 'They're hacks. And Scott Smith doesn't know what he's talking about. And neither does Stephen Petty,' And he said, 'Don't believe them.'"

NewsNation has reviewed text messages that appear to back up what Druckenbrod told us.

Though the attorneys didn't share Petty's results with residents, they did enlist a toxicologist to film a video that played for the residents.

The video was filmed by Dr. Arch "Chip" Carson, M.D., PhD., who is listed on the video as principal of Environmental Medicine Consultants. He is associated with multiple universities, including Ohio State University , the University of Cincinnati and the University of Texas School of Public Health.

In one part of the video, Dr. Carson said, "The levels that people were exposed to in the community were so small that we don't expect any kinds of cancers or health effects to have resulted from those. There will not be any long-term health impact of chemical exposure from the derailment to community members of East Palestine."

Petty told NewsNation, "The argument that there is nothing to see here is factually false. Multiple people saying there's nothing to see here … are just flat out lying or are wrong."

Mindy Bish is an attorney now representing East Palestine residents who are trying to rescind their participation in the settlement.

"Arch Carson told everyone that there was, that he would expect no cancers as a result of this exposure. No cancers. And there are cancers developing almost every week in East Palestine and someone dying of cancer almost every month," Bish told NewsNation.

"These attorneys told them that the Stephen Petty information would not support the claims. And that is not true," Bish said. "My first impressions when I saw Stephen Petty's results was this is fraudulent, this is concealment, this is manipulation."

Neither Carson nor the attorneys in the class-action settlement have responded to requests for comment from NewsNation.

Nearly 90 residents are seeking to rescind their participation in the settlement.

In part, their motion alleged "Substantial evidence of fraud and misrepresentation by class counsel, who concealed critical expert findings about health risks while inducing class members to sign personal injury releases in exchange for inadequate personal injury payments."

In April, a judge denied their effort to reopen the settlement. They have filed an appeal alleging that class counsel's own expert, Petty, held opinions materially adverse to the settlement that were not disclosed before opt-in.

"I believe I was manipulated," Druckenbord said. "I believe there was fraud. And I have the future, and my future is going to rely on proving the bad actors were wrong."

articles.title: DHS issues scathing rebuke after former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms touts cutting ties with ICE
articles.summary: Georgia gubernatorial candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms touted cutting ties with ICE as Atlanta mayor, prompting DHS to fire back with mugshots of criminals arrested in the city.
articles.body: Georgia Democratic gubernatorial candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms highlighted her past move to cut ties with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in 2018 as mayor of Atlanta, prompting a strong rebuke from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) on Monday. As Bottoms gave the keynote speech at a Democratic fundraiser in Dalton, Georgia, the former Biden official, now running for governor in the Peach State, spoke about refusing to cooperate with ICE during President Donald Trump’s first term. In her speech, she recalled her musician father’s struggle with addiction, saying that her first tour around Georgia was visiting him at various prisons. She said this helped teach her the value of "seeing the humanity in people" even those who have made mistakes or "had a different pathway to this country." "When I was mayor of Atlanta, when ICE had the family separation policy in our state, in our nation, I made the decision to end our multi-year, multi-million dollar agreement with ICE because all money ain’t good money," Bottoms said. "And when we did that, other cities followed, counties followed, other states followed and it made a difference." DEMOCRAT MAYOR BLASTED BY DHS FOR 'HUNTING DOWN' PROPERTY OWNERS LEASING TO ICE: 'UNHINGED' Fox News Digital reached out to DHS, and the department offered a scathing response to her statement. "The only difference this anti-law enforcement, pro-criminal illegal alien, former mayor made was to obstruct federal immigration laws, making Atlanta-area communities a hotbed for illegal immigration on her watch," a spokesperson for DHS said. "ICE does not separate families. Parents are asked if they want to be removed with their children or ICE will place the children with a safe person the parent designates," the statement continued. "This is consistent with past administration’s immigration enforcement." "Parents can take control of their departure with the CBP Home app and reserve the chance to come back the right legal way," the spokesperson added. "The United States is offering illegal aliens $2,600 and a free flight to self-deport now. We encourage every person here illegally to take advantage of this offer and reserve the chance to come back to the U.S. the right legal way to live the American dream. If not, you will be arrested and deported without a chance to return." NEW YORK SHERIFFS 'MAD AS HELL' AS HOCHUL PUSHES TO BAN KEY LAW ENFORCEMENT PARTNERSHIP The spokesperson made the case that cooperating with ICE is commonsense policy. "Seven of the top ten safest cities in the United States cooperate with ICE," the official continued. "Partnerships with law enforcement are critical to having the resources we need to arrest criminal illegal aliens across the country. We have had tremendous success when local law enforcement work with us, including 40,000 arrests in Florida and a two-week operation in West Virginia that resulted in the arrest of over 650 illegal aliens." "When politicians bar local law enforcement from working with DHS, our law enforcement officers have to have a more visible presence so that we can find and apprehend the criminals let out of jails and back into communities," the statement added. EXCLUSIVE: ICE NABS MULTIPLE CONVICTED KILLERS IN SINGLE DAY AMID NATIONWIDE IMMIGRATION SWEEP CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The spokesperson shared mugshots of illegal aliens arrested in Atlanta for crimes ranging from "strongarm rape" and sexual offenses toward a child to "threat-terroristic state offenses."

articles.title: Pennsylvania attorney general accuses Snapchat of failing to protect children in new lawsuit
articles.summary: Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R) announced a lawsuit Tuesday, accusing Snap, the parent company of Snapchat, of failing to protect children from...
articles.body:
Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday (R) announced a lawsuit Tuesday, accusing Snap, the parent company of Snapchat, of failing to protect children from compulsively using its platform.

The complaint , filed this week, alleges Snapchat knowingly lies about the frequency of adult-themed material like drug use or sexual content to maintain a 13+ app rating in app stores.

"Once they have you signed up and logged in, you are officially in their clutches," the attorney general said at a press conference Tuesday. "From there, Snapchat essentially says good luck getting out."

Sunday said he hopes for "honesty" from Snapchat, accusing the company's actions of violating Pennsylvania's consumer protection laws.

"The lawsuit also demands that Snapchat finally come clean about the addictiveness of their app and takes real action to protect young users," Sunday said. "This is a very serious legal action with the end goals of being an overhaul of how Snapchat markets and advertises its app."

Sunday alleged Snapchat uses functions like the Snap Streak feature, which counts the number of days two users send Snaps to one another to keep users engaged. The streak is lost when one of the users does not Snap the other in 24 hours.

"We allege this streak feature puts a tangible value on friendships and influences a child's feelings of self-worth," he said.

Sunday also argued that Snapchat's disappearing stories, messages and photos encourage users to post things they may typically not, like a revealing selfie.

The state prosecutor said parents do not have time to "fully explore" every platform and relies on "transparency" from companies when making decisions about their children's social media use.

A spokesperson for Snap stated that the allegations "fundamentally misrepresent" the platform and its approach to teen safety.

"Snapchat was designed differently from the beginning: it opens to a camera, not a feed of content, and was built to encourage self-expression and authentic connection with friends," the spokesperson told The Hill.

"We share the Attorney General's commitment to protecting young people online and are disappointed they have chosen litigation rather than working with us toward that shared goal," the spokesperson continued.

Sunday's suit comes just weeks after he announced a complaint against TikTok over similar allegations .

articles.title: ‘It’s all about her and only her’: Criticism mounts for Angel Reese after ‘selfish’ play
articles.summary: Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream are in the midst of a four-game winning streak, and on Monday night, in a win over the Los Angeles Sparks, Reese etched her...
articles.body:
Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream are in the midst of a four-game winning streak, and on Monday night, in a win over the Los Angeles Sparks , Reese etched her name in the history books. Reese snagged a record-breaking 26 rebounds in the game, the most dominant performance on the glass in the WNBA's 30-year history.

Reese also recorded yet another double-double, scoring 11 points in the contest. However, the manner in which she scored her final bucket has been deemed "unethical" by some fans.

With the outcome already decided and less than 20 seconds remaining in regulation, Reese was camped out back at the Dream's basket rather than running back to defend with her teammates, which left her wide open to collect an outlet pass and reach double-digit scoring.

"We all know Angel Reese just wants her double double and look how she gets it. Cherry picking per usual. If she doesn't get to the free throw line or cherry pick, she can't score. It's all about her and only her," posted one person on X who wan't a fan of her tactics.

We all know Angel Reese just wants her double double and look how she gets it. Cherry picking per usual. If she doesn’t get to the free throw line or cherry pick, she can’t score. It’s all about her and only her. pic.twitter.com/DS0WlKPD8u — HeHateMe (@_HeHateMee_) August 25, 2026

We all know Angel Reese just wants her double double and look how she gets it.

Cherry picking per usual. If she doesn’t get to the free throw line or cherry pick, she can’t score. It’s all about her and only her. pic.twitter.com/DS0WlKPD8u

— HeHateMe (@_HeHateMee_) August 25, 2026

The original poster wasn't alone in his criticisms of Reese.

"Even half the time she does this she blows the layup and can't score. Shoots under 50% from within a couple ft of the basket. How's that even possible? Great rebounder but she's absolutely unskilled," one fan posted on X.

"Ahhh, now I can plainly see why she misses these layups. She jumps with both feet at the same time. Why hasn't this been corrected?" another fan wondered.

"What a low IQ and selfish play. Up 7 with 15 seconds left and she doesn't run the clock out?" someone else posted.

There's no denying that Reese's offensive game needs some polishing, but even so, her impact is undeniable. Reese is on a surefire path to ending up in the Hall of Fame, and with the Dream peaking right before the playoffs, she might even beat her rival Caitlin Clark to a WNBA championship.

articles.title: Explosive diarrhea outbreak has millions of US households ditching pre-bagged salad
articles.summary: Iceberg lettuce is the only product that federal investigators have tied to outbreaks so far
articles.body:
Millions of U.S. households have stopped buying pre-bagged salad this summer following outbreaks of the explosive diarrhea-causing illness, cyclosporiasis, which has been linked to fresh produce.

Purchases of pre-bagged salad dropped 10.7 percent from June to July, totaling 6.5 million households, according to a poll of more than 3,000 fresh produce buyers by data company Numerator.

"An estimated $280 million in consumer produce spending is at risk every month the outbreak continues,' Numerator warned.

A separate July survey also found roughly 40 percent of Americans are eating or buying less fresh fruit and vegetables. On social media, posts have proliferated from Americans who say they are swearing off bagged salad to hopefully stay safe .

Cyclosporiasis has sickened at least 27,000 people in 47 states, federal data shows. Michigan health officials have reported 14,277 cases and two deaths.

The nation's largest outbreak, which started in Michigan, has been traced to produce used or sold by restaurants and retailers in dozens of states across the eastern U.S.

Cyclosporiasis is caused by the parasite cyclospora , which often hitches a ride on fresh produce. Infections can cause fever, fatigue and severe dehydration that can send people to the hospital.

Cases are hard to track because symptoms don't usually occur until two weeks after people are exposed to cyclospora .

Iceberg lettuce from a Taylor Farms facility in central Mexico was recalled in July after a U.S. Food and Drug Administration investigation tied it to an outbreak of cases at Taco Bell fast-ffod restaurants in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio and West Virginia.

The lettuce is the only produce that's been identified related to the recent o utbreaks. Past infections have been tied to other fruits and vegetables, such as raspberries and green onions.

Smaller outbreaks of unknown origin are continuing to grow, an FDA webpage shows. Missouri passed the 2,000-case mark this week. Investigations into their source are still ongoing.

There are two main steps experts say can help people stay safe. The best way to avoid the parasite is to cook food to a temperature of 158 degrees Fahrenheit.

Washing produce well – sometimes with a scrub brush – can limit the chance of exposure, but does not kill the parasite.

articles.title: Utah library confirms LGBTQ 'Pride' book for its 'smallest patrons' is kept easily accessible
articles.summary: The Provo City Library confirmed to Fox News Digital it includes "Pride is Love" and other LGBTQ board books in its collection, saying they are shelved among 2,500 titles.
articles.body: A Utah public library confirmed to Fox News Digital that an LGBTQ-themed children's book highlighted by a conservative outlet is part of its collection for its "smallest patrons" and is intentionally kept "central and easily accessible," while pushing back on claims that the book was on display. "I can confirm that the library does own a copy of ‘Pride Is Love’ along with the other small board books that were pictured in the post you referenced," Carla Z. Gordon, director of library services at Provo City Library, told Fox News Digital in a statement Tuesday. "They are not on display," Gordon added. "They are shelved in bins that contain over 2,500 other board books (any that are currently checked in). The post describes them as being 'central and easily accessible,' which is very true. These are books for our smallest patrons and we make them easy to find." OREGON SCHOOL COUNSELOR FACES BACKLASH OVER 'CHOSEN FAMILY' BOOK FOR YOUTHS On Monday, The Cougar Chronicle, which identifies itself as providing "independent conservative news and opinion at BYU," posted a photo of the book "Pride Is Love," with a caption that read, "EXCLUSIVE: The Provo City Library children's section is promoting radical gender theory, critical race theory, and other progressive propaganda to Provo's children." The thread also included photos of other LGBTQ children's books, including titles such as "Pride Puppy!," "It's a They!," "My Two Dads and Me," and another called, "My Moms Love Me." TRANSGENDER DOLLS TO BE AVAILABLE FOR MINNESOTA SCHOOLCHILDREN AS YOUNG AS 4 UNDER WALZ-BACKED PROGRAM: REPORT The Amazon page for the book, "Pride is Love," says it is intended for babies through age three and is about a girl and her two dads as they prepare to march in a Pride parade. Similarly, "My Two Dads and Me," is also intended for babies through age three and shows the day-to-day of LGBTQ fathers and their children through everyday routines, from breakfast and trips to the park, to bath time and bedtime. WASHINGTON MOTHER PULLS CHILDREN FROM SCHOOL AFTER PRIDE LESSON SHOWN IN MUSIC CLASS WITHOUT NOTICE In her statement, Gordon referenced a portion of the library’s website she said has been created to help parents select materials that match their family values. Gordon also highlighted the library’s Selection Policy, which is to "collect, organize, and make easily available to the people of the community materials which will help them in the pursuit of education, information, and the creative use of leisure time." "Within the limits of space and budget, the collection offers patrons materials in a choice of format, treatment, and level of difficulty," she added. "In this way, most individual library needs can be met and service provided to individuals of all ages." PORTLAND PARENT FIGHTS CHILD'S ELEMENTARY SCHOOL OVER 'FINAL STRAW' OF ADDING TRANS-INCLUSIVE FLAG "These particular books are not currently on display, but we do have many displays throughout the library that try to highlight books available," Gordon said. "We sometimes use holidays, observances, visiting authors, popular topics, and completely random themes all in attempt to promote our collections." "As mentioned in the Selection Policy, we do try to represent differing perspectives on many topics," she added. "Gender, sexuality, and race are all topics that have a variety of perspectives, so we do own books representing those differing voices."  "We do receive complaints from parents and community members about materials in the collection. The process is outlined in the policy referenced above," Gordon added. "When we receive these concerns, we review the materials and follow the process to either retain, move, or discard items." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Sen. Mike Lee, R-Utah, appeared to express concern about the situation in a Monday post on X, sharing the thread from The Cougar Chronicle and writing, "Come on, Provo You’re better than this."

articles.title: Ball python 'Tippy' found caged in community garden as animal control seeks owner
articles.summary: Residents and garden staff told 311 they had seen someone leave the snake in a cage beside the garden beds.
articles.body:
A routine stream of found-pet notices in Boston took an unexpected turn when city officials shared an alert for a ball python, rather than the more familiar missing dog or cat.

A caged snake later identified as "Tippy" was discovered near the raised beds of a Dorchester community food garden, Boston.com reported .

Boston Animal Care and Control said the ball python turned up at about 6 p.m. at a community garden on Ellington Street in Dorchester, per the outlet. The animal arrived there under mysterious circumstances.

Before animal control arrived, residents and garden staff told 311 they had seen someone leave the snake in a cage beside the garden beds, a spokesperson told Boston.com.

An officer brought the reptile to the city's animal care facility in Roslindale, where officials said it was in good condition and getting proper care.

They posted a photo of the reptile to their Facebook account (@bostonanimal) in hopes of finding the owner.

Ball pythons are commonly kept as pets, but they are not native to Boston and are not animals that belong outdoors in the city. Leaving one outside can put the reptile at risk, especially if it is without the temperature control, food, and shelter it needs to stay healthy.

Commenters on Facebook were wary of foul play from an owner who might have abandoned multiple pets.

"MSPCA has five of these up for adoption," one commenter noted. "Hope there's no connection."

There was immediate concern for the animal, and some disregard for whoever left it.

"OMG poor snake," another Facebook user wrote. "The person is a snake, unbelievable."

Boston.com said Tippy is being kept at the city facility in Roslindale while Boston Animal Care and Control seeks information about the snake. Anyone with details is asked to contact the agency at 617-635-1800 or animalshelter@boston.gov.

Until then, the ball python remains in city care.

In general, if pet owners are unable to take care of a pet, leaving the animal outside should not be the next move.

Instead, contacting local shelters and care facilities that might be able to rehome and host the pets is a much better option for the animal and the local community.

articles.title: Chicago Cubs vs. Arizona Diamondbacks preview, Tuesday 8/25, 8:40 CT
articles.summary: The Cubs go for the series win.
articles.body:
NIGHT MOVES: The Cubs ' win last night made their record 29-16 under the lights on the road. They wound up 29-20 in such games a year ago. They now have as many wins this year on the road as at home: 38. They have lost 29 on the road and 27 at home. (Courtesy BCB's JohnW53)

WINNERS AND LOSERS: The Cubs are 35-26 in games against opponents who had a winning record going into the game. They are 41-30 against those who were .500 or below. (Courtesy BCB's JohnW53)

RUN DIFFERENTIAL UPDATE: The Cubs have outscored the Mariners and Diamondbacks by a combined 26-0 over the last 16 innings. They have raised their run differential to a season-high +122. Only two teams are better: the Brewers , +161, and Dodgers , +151. The Braves are fourth, at +110. (Courtesy BCB's JohnW53)

BATTING AVERAGE UPDATE: In their last 54 games, one third of a full season, the Cubs have raised their batting average with runners in scoring position by 32 points, to .249, which is tied for seventh highest. They now have scored the second-most runs, made the third-most hits, hit the most home runs and earned the second-most walks. With two outs and RISP, they rank 14th in average, at .233. They have scored the most runs, made the second-most hits, hit the most home runs and earned the third-most walks. (Courtesy BCB's JohnW53)

TODAY IN CUBS HISTORY: Ryne Sandberg's 12th-inning single gives the Cubs a 4-3 walk-off win over the Braves. They lead the NL East by two games. It happened 37 years ago today, Friday, Aug. 25, 1989 .

Night two in AZ. Tune in live on @WatchMarquee . pic.twitter.com/iXAJXa2o7R — Chicago Cubs (@Cubs) August 25, 2026

Night two in AZ. Tune in live on @WatchMarquee . pic.twitter.com/iXAJXa2o7R

Pfaadt on the mound. pic.twitter.com/lS5sTSLHsP — Arizona Diamondbacks (@Dbacks) August 25, 2026

Pfaadt on the mound. pic.twitter.com/lS5sTSLHsP

Clay Holmes , RHP vs. Brandon Pfaadt , RHP

After a bit of a rough outing in his Cubs debut, Clay Holmes has been lights-out over his last two: 12 innings, one run, 26 ground-ball outs out of 36 total outs recorded (and 45 batters faced).

That's exactly who the Cubs thought they were getting.

He has not faced the Diamondbacks since a relief appearance in early 2024 and current D-backs are batting a small sample size .216 (8-for-37) with no home runs.

Brandon Pfaadt has a 1.79 ERA and 0.912 WHIP in 10 starts since June 30, though he did get hit hard (five runs in 5.2 innings) by the Red Sox in his most recent start Aug. 19 .

He allowed the Cubs two runs in 2.1 innings in a relief appearance at Wrigley Field May 3 .

Current Cubs are batting just .165 (14-for-85) against him, though Michael Conforto has homered twice.

Today's game is on Marquee Sports Network. It's also streaming on Peacock (outside the Cubs and Diamondbacks market territories).

Here is the complete MLB.com live streaming page for today.

Please visit our SB Nation Diamondbacks site AZ Snakepit . If you do go there to interact with D-backs fans, please be respectful, abide by their individual site rules and serve as a good representation of Cub fans in general and BCB in particular.

The 2026 game discussion procedure has been changed, so please take note.

You'll find the game preview, like this one, posted separately on the front page two hours before game time (90 minutes for some early day games following night games).

At the same time, a StoryStream containing the preview will also post on the front page, titled "Cubs vs. (Team) (Day of week/date) game threads." It will contain every post related to that particular game.

The Live! (formerly "First Pitch") thread will still post at five minutes to game time. It will also post to the front page. That will be the only live game discussion thread. After the game, the recap and Heroes and Goats will also live on the front page as separate posts.

You will also be able to find the preview, Live! thread, recap and Heroes and Goats in this section link . The StoryStream for each game can also be found in that section.

articles.title: ‘My main goal is to help people’: I’m single, 74, with $10 million burning a hole in my pocket. What should I do?
articles.summary: “I also own my home and an SUV outright, with no outstanding debt.”
articles.body:
I am a single, healthy 74-year-old woman. I have never been married and I have no children. I currently live in Texas and plan to donate most, if not all, of my assets to charity after I pass away.

At present, I have four brokerage accounts — two individual accounts, one self-directed IRA and one self-directed Roth IRA — as well as several online bank accounts. Altogether, these accounts total a little over $10 million.

Dick's Sporting Goods' epic drop hits other footwear giants, as shoppers sour on retro sneakers

Trump's trade war with Canada could lead the U.S. back to quantitative easing

Instead of hiring an attorney to establish a revocable living trust or prepare a formal will, can I simply name different charitable organizations as beneficiaries on all of my financial accounts? I could also handwrite a last will and testament explaining my wishes.

One part of me would like to leave my house and SUV to my niece and nephew, because they are both willing to serve as my financial and medical powers of attorney and to help carry out my wishes after my death.

However, another part of me would actually prefer to donate the house and SUV to charity. My concern is that I need someone I trust to serve as my financial and medical powers of attorney and to handle the administration of my estate.

My main goal is to help people who are poor and in need. If my niece and nephew receive the house and SUV, I would probably ask them to donate half of the proceeds to the Red Cross. I am also preparing my tax return now.

I also own my home and SUV outright, with no outstanding debt. I have already prepaid my funeral expenses. I would like to simplify my estate planning if possible. In particular, I would appreciate advice about:

1. How to properly arrange for my niece and nephew to serve as my financial and medical powers of attorney. Who should serve as executor or otherwise handle my estate after my death?

2. Is a handwritten will legally sufficient and advisable in Texas?

3. Will there be additional tax returns or other tax obligations that need to be handled after I die? If so, who would be responsible for filing them? Are there tax advantages or disadvantages to leaving my assets directly to charities?

I would very much appreciate any suggestions you have. How do you think I should proceed?

Related: 'This is a tricky subject': We're in our 70s and our only child is 40. Do we leave her everything?

You know what you want. The rest is logistics.
